nonBlockingNotes: AC7 ('all qrspi CLI commands emit to the CLI log') is covered by the shared importable logger module, but the design openly flags via OQ4 that wiring the ~40 standalone scripts + skills may exceed this ticket's scope. Defensible explicitly-stated deferral; a downstream reviser should confirm whether 'deliver the module, adopt incrementally' satisfies the AC's 'all commands' wording.

AC4's 'backoff' sub-requirement is covered honestly: backoff_seconds recorded as 0/null because Q7 proves no backoff policy exists, escalated via OQ1. Addressed rather than dropped; human confirmation that a placeholder value is acceptable interim coverage is worth getting.

AC2 names a single repo-root events.jsonl as the write path; the design satisfies it as a read target via run-start aggregation while events are written per-worktree. Covered-and-justified reinterpretation, but the freshness contract (OQ2) is a semantic narrowing a decision-maker should sign off on.

Dangling self-reference: line 29 states it is 'correcting the earlier always-recorded treatment in the error-event behavior above', but line 24 already declares traceback debug-only. No 'always-recorded' treatment exists to correct, so the cross-reference is stale; drop or rewrite it.

Rotation/retention coverage is asymmetric and undefined for cli.log: rotation (line 26) and retention (line 27) are described only for the per-worktree events.jsonl, yet line 48 gitignores the repo-root cli.log alongside archive/, implying cli.log is rotated. No rotation/retention behavior is specified for cli.log (likely entangled with the blocking concurrency finding).

Enum member phase_end (line 22 enum) is never described as emitted; OQ3 acknowledges the documented superset, so not a dangling reference, but the unfired member is worth confirming during implementation.

Decision 2 (Option B) changes the event-log WRITE target away from the ticket's literally-named path (lines 11/14/54). The design writes per-worktree and makes the repo-root path an aggregated read target rebuilt at run start. Real deviation but defensibly grounded in Q10, preserves the read contract at the named path, openly surfaced as Decision 2 / OQ2 confirm-only.

AC line 68 ('all qrspi CLI commands emit') is not fully committed in the Delta (only qrspi_cli_logger.py + orchestrator, not the ~40 scripts). Disclosed as OQ4 grounded in Q6; advisory, but a decider should confirm whether 'all commands' requires the wiring in-scope.
backoff_seconds recorded as 0/null because Q7 shows the ticket's backoff premise is false; surfaced as OQ1 + risk rather than fabricated. Correct handling.
retry_attempt reclassified from event_type (ticket line 24) to context field (ticket line 35) to resolve the ticket's own contradiction; disclosed minor schema clarification.

Decision 2 (Option B) adds a moving part (qrspi_event_aggregate.py + run-start shell-out) a literal single-path design would not need. Defensible: Q10 confirms path-isolation concurrency with zero locking, and Option B reuses that rather than introducing fcntl.flock (Option C) — the simpler-of-alternatives choice. Value depends on the OQ2 freshness contract being acceptable.
Seven new Python modules + schema is a sizeable surface, but each maps to a distinct AC and follows the one-concern-per-script convention; proportional AC-aligned decomposition, not over-engineering.

Two-tiered log-level filtering (record drop + field strip of debug-only fields like context.traceback) is more than a single threshold check, but is tied directly to ticket line 69 which record-level dropping alone cannot satisfy — demanded by the AC, not gratuitous.

Decision 2 Option B's run-start aggregation gives the repo-root read target a freshness contract of 'current as of the last run start' (stale between aggregations within a run). Flagged confirm-only (OQ2). Verified plausible against the sequential single-process batch loop — not a node-validity defect, but a real operability tradeoff for any consumer reading the aggregated events.jsonl mid-run.

The traceback field is described as always-present in the error-event bullet (line 24) then re-classified as debug-only in the log-level bullet (line 29), which the document calls out as a self-correction. Coherent on net but reads inconsistently in isolation; a consistency nit.

Per-event subprocess on every transition (Decision 1, mirroring qrspi_metrics_append.py shelled out via engineCmd) is the verified-real precedent but adds one spawn per event. Risk Register already notes this (med/med) with 'batch within a do* return where possible'; consistent with established practice.

AC 'all qrspi commands emit to the CLI log' is covered by the shared importable logger (qrspi_cli_logger.py), but the design defers wiring the ~40 scripts + skills to OQ4 as possibly-out-of-scope. Module delivered; whether 'all commands' actually emit at ticket close is left open. Defensible (no single CLI chokepoint per Q6), but a decider should resolve OQ4 so the AC's 'all commands' literal is not ambiguous.

AC 'Every retry generates ... backoff' is covered partially in substance: retry_attempt from the CI-Revise-Attempt trailer, backoff_seconds 0/null because no pipeline backoff source exists (ticket premise contradicted by Q7). Surfaced honestly as Risk + OQ1 rather than dropped; defensible deferral, not a coverage gap.

Mild framing tension (non-contradictory): the events.jsonl bullet says the emitter writes 'mirroring the metrics-ledger writer' (which Q9 says does NOT flush/fsync), while the Risk Register prescribes adding explicit flush()+os.fsync(). Reconciled in-text (labeled 'new behavior beyond the ledger precedent'), but the Delta entry for qrspi_event_log.py omits the flush/fsync behavior, leaving the durability contract stated in only one place.
secrets.token_hex arity given specifically as token_hex(8) only at line 89; lines 32/40 write it without the argument. Not a mismatch, but the per-event event_id length is pinned in one location.

Decision 2 and the Risk Register assert a codebase mechanism research does not establish: that doLand reaps the worktree via `git worktree remove --force` in qrspi_cleanup.py within the same run. Q8/Q10 establish worktree isolation and git-common-dir → main checkout, but neither qrspi_cleanup.py nor doLand's removal timing appears in research.md. Non-blocking because the chosen Option A does not depend on the reaping claim (used only to reject Option B); the chosen design rests on the research-grounded git-common-dir resolution. Recommend softening the claim or verifying it.

The design states datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() is 'the exact idiom qrspi_metrics_append.py:133 already uses'. Q14 confirms Python tools mint a wall-clock timestamp, but the specific line number / exact idiom string are not quoted in research.md — minor precision claim slightly beyond the cited evidence. Non-material.

Decision 2 is an exemplary simplicity case: it explicitly rejects the aggregator (Option B) and the fcntl.flock lock (Option C) as machinery that solves a race the sequential single-process batch loop never produces, defers flock to OQ2, and writes directly to a single repo-root JSONL sink mirroring qrspi_metrics_append.py. No simpler alternative skipped.

The trace_id/span_id/parent_span_id model is new but justified, not scope creep: Q2 (derived from the ticket) explicitly names span_id and parent_span_id as required event-schema fields, and it is built on the existing crypto-guarded id idiom rather than a new mechanism.

The only mechanism exceeding existing precedent is the explicit flush()+os.fsync() in the emitter (no fsync anywhere in the repo). Defensible against the ticket's 'flushed-before-continue' wording and flagged in the Risk Register; not blocking but the one place the design adds durability machinery with no in-repo precedent.

Verified the central Option A worktree-survival claim against real source: qrspi_paths._git_common_dir (scripts/qrspi_paths.py:57-78) returns the shared .git parent (MAIN checkout root) even from a linked worktree, and resolve_repo_root uses it. The events.jsonl path <root>/.qrspi/observability/events.jsonl is a SIBLING of .worktrees/, not under it; qrspi_cleanup.py reaps only <root>/.worktrees/<ticket> via `git worktree remove --force`. So the canonical log provably survives worktree reaping. CORRECT.

Subtle precision the design gets right: qrspi_metrics_append.py uses the SAME resolve_repo_root but then joins .worktrees/<id>/.qrspi/<id>/, so the metrics ledger itself lives INSIDE the reaped worktree tree — NOT a survives-cleanup precedent for the repo-root path. The design's survival guarantee rests on its DIFFERENT (repo-root, non-worktree) subpath. The 'exactly like qrspi_metrics_append.py' prose is accurate only about the root-resolution mechanism, not the final sink location; real-but-non-material imprecision.

Decision 2's critique of rejected Option B (run-start aggregation loses terminal land/phase_success events because doLand reaps the per-worktree file in the same run) is verified correct: a per-worktree events.jsonl WOULD live under .worktrees/<id> and be destroyed by the same `git worktree remove --force`.

Decision 4 nested-config precedent verified (qrspi_critics_config.py is a real purpose-built nested-block resolver); timestamp idiom verified at qrspi_metrics_append.py:133; gitignore state verified (only .qrspi/config.json + .qrspi/features/ + .worktrees/ ignored), so the new-.gitignore-entry requirement is real.
The design honestly flags the ticket's false backoff premise as OQ1 with backoff_seconds 0/null — consistent with Q7 and the real code. Sound treatment of a wrong upstream premise, not a node defect.

AC7 ('Interactive mode: logs also emit to stderr at info level or above') is covered as a behavior, but the design never specifies HOW interactive vs non-interactive (batch) mode is detected — the distinction Q14 raised. The stderr-only routing rule answers Q14's stdout-corruption concern, so not a coverage gap, but interactive-detection is left implicit.

AC4's 'backoff' half is covered only as an explicit deferral: backoff_seconds recorded as 0/null because no pipeline backoff policy exists (Risk + OQ1). Defensible documented deferral, not a silent drop, but resolution depends on the human answering OQ1.

AC7's scope ('ALL qrspi CLI commands emit') is delivered as a shared logger module for incremental adoption rather than wired into all ~40 scripts/skills; surfaced explicitly as OQ4 rather than silently narrowed.

fsync framing tension (self-disclosed): line 23 says the emitter writes one JSON line 'mirroring the metrics-ledger writer' (which does NO flush/fsync), while the Risk Register (line 106) prescribes adding explicit flush()+os.fsync() as 'new behavior beyond the ledger precedent'. Reconcilable and explicitly flagged, but line 23's 'mirroring' could note durability is added on top.

Retry event-type notation: line 22 lists doRevise's bump as '(retry/retry_attempt)' (reads like two event types), whereas line 25 establishes the retry event TYPES as 'retry' + 'error_retry' with retry_attempt being a FIELD. Intent clear from line 25; line 22 is loose notation.

Config-key naming presentation: logSizeThreshold (line 26) and logRetentionDays (line 27) appear bare while logLevel is written 'observability.logLevel' (line 29). Decision 4 / Delta unambiguously nest all three under observability.*, so no real ambiguity — only inconsistent shorthand.

AC7 ('all qrspi CLI commands emit structured logs') is mapped to a shared importable logger module rather than wiring all ~40 scripts/skills, because Q6 established no single CLI chokepoint. Not silently narrowed — raised as OQ4 for human decision. Advisory; should be resolved before/at structure phase so AC7 is not under-delivered.

The design relocates the ticket's literal single repo-root events.jsonl onto a flock-guarded shared path (Decision 2 Option C) and flags via OQ2 that this clashes with the per-worktree path-isolation model (Q10). Honors the ticket's stated path while honestly surfacing the concurrency cost; introduces a net-new locking pattern, correctly marked NEW PATTERN with justification.

Decision 2 adopts a brand-new fcntl.flock locking primitive (NEW PATTERN, zero codebase precedent per Q10) when the simpler Option B (per-worktree events.jsonl + run-start aggregation) would inherit existing path-isolation for free and need no lock. Rationale (the ticket literally names a single repo-root path) is defensible and surfaced as OQ2, so not blocking; but if the reviewer accepts a per-worktree log, the entire locking concern and POSIX-only flock dependency disappear — materially simpler.

The Delta adds six new Python modules plus six test siblings. Proportional — each maps to a distinct AC (emit, rotate, retention, CLI-leveled-logging, nested-config, schema/enum) and follows the one-tool-per-script + _test.py convention — not over-decomposition. Noted only so a reviewer can confirm none of the smaller modules (rotation vs retention) are worth co-locating.

Decision 3 recommends span_id/parent_span_id follow 'Option A's crypto pattern (like runId)', i.e. the JS crypto-guarded no-Date.now()/Math.random() idiom — but Decision 1 puts the emitter in Python, where span ids would most naturally be minted with Python stdlib (uuid4/secrets) and the JS-only prohibition does not apply. Under-specification of WHERE span ids are generated, not a false claim; structure/plan can resolve it.

Risk register row 'Per-event subprocess on a hot path' proposes 'batch within a do* return where possible', but the primary emission model (Decision 1 Option A: orchestrator shells out at each transition) inherently means one python3 subprocess per event. Mild tension; not blocking since the durable-event-log goal is met regardless, and the metrics ledger (qrspi-batch.js:980) already establishes the same per-step shell-out cost as acceptable precedent.

The `phase_end` event_type appears in the authoritative enum but no emission site is named for it (the `do*` returns map to `phase_success`/`phase_failure`/`phase_skip`); defensibly covered by OQ3 (schema documents the full superset while only a subset fires today), so non-blocking, but a reviser could state explicitly where `phase_end` fires versus `phase_success`.

The `status` enum (`ok`, `error`, `skipped`) from the ticket is referenced as 'validated against a fixed enum' but the design does not spell out the status-to-event_type mapping (e.g. which event_types carry `skipped`); coverage is present but the mapping is left implicit.

`backoff_seconds` is honestly carried as sourceless via OQ1 (record 0/null and document the gap); defensibly covers the ticket's retry-AC mention of backoff given the upstream premise is inaccurate per Q7, but remains an open decision a human must close.

The Desired End State states '`event_type` and `status` are validated against a fixed enum,' but only the `event_type` enum is ever enumerated; the `status` field's enum/allowed values are never defined anywhere. Under-specification (a completeness gap), not an internal contradiction, so it does not fail the consistency lens, but the `status` enum should be pinned down before structure/implementation.

Config-key presentation is uneven: `observability.logLevel` is written fully-qualified while `logSizeThreshold`/`logRetentionDays` appear bare. All three are clearly intended to live under the single `observability.*` block, so this is a naming-presentation inconsistency, not a contract mismatch.
Decision-heading style is mixed: Decisions 2/5/6/7 use 'Decision (committed)' while Decisions 1/3/4 use 'Recommendation'. Every option is unambiguously resolved, so cosmetic, not a contradiction.

Decision 7 asserts the metrics-ledger writer uses `datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()` 'verbatim' at `scripts/qrspi_metrics_append.py:133`. The research confirms the ledger carries a `timestamp` envelope field and is the JSONL precedent, but the quoted research evidence does not literally show that exact expression/line number. Defensible elaboration, not contradicted, but the specific line-133 citation is more precise than the research substantiates — worth a reviser spot-check, not a blocker.

Decision 6 introduces the literals `"orchestrator"` and `"user"`/`"cli"` for non-agent emission paths. These are greenfield values with no research anchor (Q3 only establishes `agentType`/label as real proxies). A reasonable, honestly-labeled NEW PATTERN derivation rather than an unsupported codebase-fact claim, so non-blocking — but the design is asserting a convention, not a discovered fact.

Decision 2 introduces fcntl.flock locking, which has zero precedent (path isolation is the codebase's sole concurrency model and the batch loop is sequential). The design justifies it with a concrete cross-invocation race scenario and chooses it as the minimal guard for the ticket's committed single shared path, so it is defensible justified complexity. Worth noting only because the simpler Option B (per-worktree path + run-start aggregation) would inherit the existing isolation for free; the design rejects it solely to honor the ticket's literal path, a reasonable but reviewer-checkable tradeoff.

Decisions 5 (event_id via uuid.uuid4), 6 (actor via call-site-supplied agentType/'orchestrator'/'user'), and 7 (timestamp via datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()) are each minimal and proportional: a single stdlib call or a thin required argument, all grounded in real available identifiers or the verbatim existing metrics-ledger idiom. No over-engineering in any of the three.

Decision 5/6/7 all verify clean against real source. event_id: no Python id-gen idiom exists in scripts/; uuid.uuid4() is stdlib and draws from os.urandom, so the clock-independent/resume-irrelevant claim is correct. timestamp: datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat() is the verbatim idiom at scripts/qrspi_metrics_append.py:133 (confirmed). The design's scoping of the Date.now()/Math.random() prohibition to the JS workflow sandbox is correct — that ban is documented at qrspi-batch.js:115-117 and does not bind a Python subprocess. actor grounds on the real agentType identifier — sound.

The Risk Register's fsync row and Decision 2's flock guard add durability/concurrency behavior BEYOND the qrspi_metrics_append.py precedent the design otherwise mirrors. Correctly acknowledged as new behavior, but fsync+flock are net-new machinery with no in-repo precedent — the implementation carries more novelty than 'mirrors the ledger writer' implies. Not blocking; mechanisms are standard stdlib.

Decision 2 commits a repo-root shared events.jsonl guarded by fcntl.flock, justified by a concurrent-cross-invocation-batch race. That race is real (resolve_repo_root resolves git-common-dir first, verified), but today's single batch run is sequential, so the guard protects a not-yet-existing concurrent-invocation usage. Defensible (honors the ticket's stated single path) but the flock machinery solves a latent rather than present race — a noteworthy tradeoff, not an error.
